defects: hM_proper : I • M ≠ ⊤ is not meaningfully typed as written: M is a bare Type* with a Module R M instance, not a Submodule R M, so 'I • M' cannot denote the submodule I·M (should be I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) as in gold); as stated this hypothesis does not correctly express 'I·M is a proper submodule of M'

hExt : ∀ i < n, CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext i N M = 0 is not well-typed: Ext i N M (Mathlib's Abelian.Ext) is a Type-valued Hom-object, not an element of an additive group, so comparing it to '0' via '=' does not typecheck; the gold correctly expresses vanishing via Subsingleton (Ext N M i)

Conclusion's ∀ k, IsRegular (seq k) drops the module M entirely: unqualified IsRegular in Mathlib is the ring/monoid notion of a non-zero-divisor element of R, unrelated to M, so this fails to express 'M-regular sequence' — it neither references M nor captures the required successive-quotient regularity condition (r_1 regular on M, r_2 regular on M/(r_1)M, etc.) that the gold's IsRegular M rs encodes

Support hypothesis coerces I to Set R explicitly via (↑I : Set R) versus gold's implicit Ideal coercion — cosmetic, not a defect, but flagged since combined with the Ext/regularity issues the overall statement is not a faithful formalization
